verses.text: Then King Solomon called together in Jerusalem the leaders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes and the chiefs of the families of Israel. He wanted them to bring up the ark of the LORD's covenant from Zion, the City of David.
All the men of Israel gathered before King Solomon at the festival in the month of Ethanim, the seventh month.
When all the leaders of Israel had arrived, the priests lifted up the ark.
They brought up the LORD's ark, the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy things that were in the tent. The priests and Levites carried them up.
King Solomon and all the people of Israel who had gathered with him stood in front of the ark. They sacrificed so many sheep and cattle that no one could count them.
Then the priests carried the ark of the LORD's covenant to its place in the inner room of the temple, the Most Holy Place, and put it under the wings of the winged creatures.
The winged creatures spread their wings over the place where the ark was, and covered the ark and its carrying poles from above.
The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Holy Place in front of the inner room, but not from outside. They are still there today.
There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets Moses had put there at Mount Horeb. That is where the LORD made a covenant with the people of Israel after they came out of Egypt.
When the priests came out of the Holy Place, a cloud filled the LORD's temple.
The priests could not stay to do their work because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled his temple.
Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would live in thick darkness.
But I have built a wonderful temple for you, a place where you can live forever."
Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel while they stood there.
He said, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel! With his own mouth he made a promise to my father David, and with his own hand he has kept it. He said,
'Since the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel to build a temple for my name. But I have chosen David to rule my people Israel.'
My father David wanted with all his heart to build a temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to my father David, 'You wanted with all your heart to build a temple for my name, and it was good that you wanted to.
But you are not the one to build the temple. Your own son will build the temple for my name.'

Now the LORD has kept the promise he made. I have taken my father David's place, and I sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised. And I have built the temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
I have made a place there for the ark, which holds the LORD's covenant. That is the covenant he made with our ancestors when he brought them out of Egypt."
Then Solomon stood in front of the LORD's altar, facing all the people of Israel. He spread out his hands toward heaven
and said: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below. You keep your covenant and show your faithful love to your servants who follow you with all their heart.
You have kept your promise to your servant, my father David. With your own mouth you promised, and with your own hand you have done it, as we see today.

So now, LORD, God of Israel, keep the other promise you made to your servant, my father David. You said, 'You will always have a descendant sitting before me on the throne of Israel, if your sons are careful to live before me as you have done.'
So now, God of Israel, please let the promise you made to your servant, my father David, come true.
But will God really live on earth? Even the highest heavens cannot hold you. How much less this temple I have built!
But please listen to your servant's prayer and his request, LORD my God. Hear the cry and the prayer your servant is praying to you today.
May your eyes watch over this temple night and day, this place where you said, 'My name will be there.' May you hear the prayer your servant prays toward this place.
Listen to the requests of your servant and your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, where you live, and when you hear, forgive.
If someone wrongs his neighbour and is made to take an oath, and he comes and takes the oath in front of your altar in this temple,
then hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants. Punish the guilty person as he deserves, and show that the innocent person is not guilty, as he deserves.
When your people Israel are defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against you, and then they turn back to you, praise your name, and pray and beg you in this temple,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel. Bring them back to the land you gave to their ancestors.
When the sky is shut and there is no rain because your people have sinned against you, and then they pray toward this place, praise your name, and turn from their sin because you have punished them,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave your people as their own.

When there is famine or deadly disease in the land, or when the crops are ruined by disease or mould, locusts or grasshoppers, or when enemies surround one of their cities, whatever disaster or sickness comes,
and when any of your people Israel pray or ask for help, each one knowing the pain in his own heart, and spreading out his hands toward this temple,
then hear from heaven, where you live. Forgive and act. Deal with each person according to everything he does, since you know his heart. For you alone know the hearts of all people.
Then they will respect you all the time they live in the land you gave to our ancestors.
And foreigners who are not from your people Israel may come from far away because of your name.
They will hear about your great name, your mighty hand, and your powerful arm. When they come and pray toward this temple,

then hear from heaven, where you live, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you. Then all the peoples of the earth will know your name and respect you, as your people Israel do. They will know that this temple I have built is called by your name.
When your people go out to fight against their enemies, wherever you send them, and when they pray to the LORD toward the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name,
then hear their prayer and their requests from heaven, and help them win their cause.

When they sin against you, for there is no one who does not sin, and you become angry with them and hand them over to their enemies, who take them away as prisoners to the enemy's land, far away or near,
then if they change their hearts in the land where they are prisoners, and turn back and beg you there, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'

and if they come back to you with all their heart and soul in the land of the enemies who took them away, and pray to you toward the land you gave their ancestors, toward the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name,
then hear their prayer and their requests from heaven, where you live, and help them win their cause.
Forgive your people who have sinned against you. Forgive all the wrongs they have done against you. Make those who captured them show them mercy.
For they are your people and your own special possession. You brought them out of Egypt, out of that furnace for melting iron.
May your eyes be open to the requests of your servant and of your people Israel. May you listen to them whenever they cry out to you.
For you chose them out of all the peoples of the earth to be your own special possession, as you said through your servant Moses when you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, Lord GOD."
When Solomon finished praying all this prayer and these requests to the LORD, he stood up in front of the LORD's altar, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.
He stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, saying in a loud voice:
"Praise the LORD! He has given rest to his people Israel, just as he promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises he gave through his servant Moses.
May the LORD our God be with us, as he was with our ancestors. May he never leave us or give up on us.
May he turn our hearts toward him, so that we will follow all his ways and keep the commands, laws, and rules he gave our ancestors.
And may these words I have prayed to the LORD stay near the LORD our God day and night. May he help his servant and his people Israel with whatever each day needs.
Then all the peoples of the earth will know that the LORD is God, and there is no other.
So you must be completely faithful to the LORD our God. Follow his laws and keep his commands, as you are doing today."
Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices to the LORD.
Solomon offered peace offerings to the LORD: twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people of Israel dedicated the LORD's temple.

On that same day the king made holy the middle part of the courtyard in front of the LORD's temple. There he offered the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar in front of the LORD was too small to hold them all.

So Solomon and all Israel with him celebrated the festival at that time. It was a great crowd of people who came from as far as Lebo Hamath in the north and the stream of Egypt in the south. They celebrated before the LORD our God for seven days and then seven more days, fourteen days in all.
On the next day he sent the people home. They blessed the king and went home happy and glad in their hearts for all the good things the LORD had done for his servant David and for his people Israel.
